# Municipal Report Management System — Fully English Variant

This repository is the fully English, standalone variant of the GR10 Software Engineering project. Production code, tests, Java types and filenames, GUI bindings, persistence identifiers, database schema names, configuration, and stable application values use English conventions.

## Overview

The application manages citizen reports about municipal problems and service disruptions. Citizens can register, submit reports, and review their submissions. Municipal operators can review received reports, assign and advance report status, add internal notes, and monitor activity trends.

The implementation follows the BCED organization:

- `Boundary`: Swing user interfaces
- `Control`: use-case controllers
- `Entity`: domain entities, services, and report-state classes
- `Database`: JPA persistence support

The report lifecycle consistently uses `Submitted → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved`.

## Requirements

- Java 23
- Maven
- MySQL

## MySQL setup

The English variant uses a distinct schema and credentials:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE reports_db;
CREATE USER 'reports_user'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'reports_password';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON reports_db.* TO 'reports_user'@'localhost';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;
```

The matching defaults in `src/main/resources/META-INF/persistence.xml` are:

```xml
<property name="jakarta.persistence.jdbc.url" value="jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/reports_db"/>
<property name="jakarta.persistence.jdbc.user" value="reports_user"/>
<property name="jakarta.persistence.jdbc.password" value="reports_password"/>
```

Change the example password in both MySQL and `persistence.xml` for any non-local environment. The English persistence unit is `Municipal_Report_Management_System`; JPA creates and updates the English table and column schema.

## Build and test

```shell
mvn test
```

content.text:
I wrote two PlantUML views and a README to `task2view-out/GR10-Q4/`. I did not render the diagrams, so they are untested.

- **`view-1.puml` (use case view):** it shows the two roles a user picks at registration, Citizen and Municipal Operator, plus the visitor who hasn't signed in yet.
  - **Citizen goals:** report a problem, view their own submitted reports with details and history, and see status-change notifications.
  - **Operator goals:** view and filter received reports, advance a report's status, add internal notes, and monitor activity trends.
  - **How they connect:** report lists open the details screen, notes are added from the details, and a status update can trigger a notification.
- **`view-2.puml` (activity view):** it follows one report from creation to closure across the roles. A citizen creates it as Submitted. An operator reviews it, optionally annotates it, and moves it Submitted → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved. Citizens are notified only on Assigned and Resolved, and a Resolved report can't be changed again. Monitoring is a separate operator-only summary across all reports.

The README says what each view shows and why, and notes two quirks in the code. A status update advances one step; the operator can't pick the target status. Some of the report-creation validation rules are hard-coded sample values.
